profile.doc_version: derived from live capture (no vendor doc yet)
profile.description: Zenithra Ax1 sCAN ASCII/CSV protocol. The base packet is AIS-140 (India VLT mandate); over and above it the sentence carries the vehicle CAN bus inline as one field of ';'-separated <hex id>:<hex payload> frames. Comma-delimited sentences framed by $MMI,...*CC, one sentence per message, 38 fields. Wired into the live codec runway/codecs/zenithra.py (which derives from the AIS-140 codec); data/protocols/zenithra.py is the standalone transferable parser.
profile.downlink: The server -> device command set is not documented yet. The device is AIS-140-derived so the AIS-140 catalogue (see ais140.json ota_commands, e.g. +S*R:SET:VRN#...;) is the likely superset, but no command has been confirmed on this model — no ota_commands are declared here on purpose, so no unverified command is offered for sending.

checksum.note: Carried through verbatim, NOT verified. The two captured sentences end in *A4 and *46, which match no standard XOR or additive checksum over the sentence body (or any substring of it common to both), so the field is informational/vendor-specific — same situation as the AIS-140 spec's own examples.

framing.line_terminator: CRLF in the capture; the parser accepts CR/LF/none.

dispatch.rule: strip the leading '$', split on ',' — token[0] is the header and token[1:] are its fields (1-based index in each packet type's field list below). The device opens the connection with an AIS-140 'LGN' login (confirmed) and then sends 'MMI' data sentences. Health (HLP/HEL) and emergency (EPB) have not been captured on this model; if they appear, see ais140.json for their grammar.

headers.LGN: login (sent once per connection, before any data)
headers.MMI: normal + alert packet (with optional CAN payload)

dispatch.identification: The login is a plain AIS-140 $LGN and is NOT enough on its own to tell this device from a Locate 140B — except for field 4, the protocol-version literal, which is 'SCAN' here where AIS-140 sends 'AIS140'. Any tool that picks a parser from the first packet of a connection must key on that literal, or it will lock onto AIS-140 and then fail to parse every $MMI sentence that follows.

LGN.name: Login Packet
LGN.description: First packet sent immediately after the TCP connection is established. The AIS-140 login minus its vendor_id field, so IMEI and firmware sit one slot earlier than the AIS-140 v1.9 doc's 9-field layout — locate the IMEI by content (a 14-16 digit run) rather than by fixed position if both layouts must parse.

fields.name: firmware_version
fields.note: x.y.z with an optional build letter

fields.name: protocol_version
fields.note: 'SCAN' — the Ax1 sCAN mode, and the only field that identifies this device family at login time (AIS-140 sends 'AIS140' here)

MMI.name: Normal / Alert Packet
MMI.description: Regular tracking packet, sent at the configured interval or on an alert; the same layout carries every alert subtype via packet_type + alert_id. The CAN field (36) is empty when the bus has nothing to report, so the field count is 38 either way.
MMI.server_response: +##Received OK (assumed from the AIS-140 base — not yet confirmed on this model)
MMI.note: Fields 1-25 are the AIS-140 v1.9 normal-packet head field for field, except field 1 (a packet-format version here, not a vendor id). From field 26 the layouts diverge: AIS-140's emergency_status (its 26) is not sent, so everything after shifts one slot earlier; the 4 neighbour-cell triples (AIS-140 33-44) and the odometer (its 50) are not sent; the CAN field is new; and frame_number moves to the very end, after the OTA field. Field 37 (ota_update_details) is a parenthesized, comma-separated triple, so it must NOT be split on ',' with the rest — fold from '(' to ')' before indexing, and note that (unlike AIS-140) it is not the last field.

fields.name: packet_version
fields.note: packet-format version. AIS-140 carries a vendor_id in this slot; the only vendor token here is the $MMI header itself.

fields.name: alert_id
fields.note: see message_alert_ids; 1/2 are routine location updates, 3-16 are alerts

fields.name: network_operator
fields.note: may contain a space; never a comma

fields.name: tamper_alert
fields.note: PROVISIONAL: read as AIS-140's tamper_alert (its field 27) because the captured value is the letter 'O', which matches that field's documented C/O value set — i.e. AIS-140's emergency_status (its 26, a 0/1 flag) is taken to be the field this protocol drops. Confirm against the vendor doc; if it is in fact emergency_status, this slot and the codec's io key both need renaming.

fields.name: digital_input_status
fields.note: bit meanings assumed from the AIS-140 base — not confirmed on this model

fields.name: can_data
fields.note: This protocol's addition to the AIS-140 base — the vehicle CAN bus, inline. Empty when there is nothing to report. See the can_data section for the grammar.

fields.name: ota_update_details
fields.note: '()' when idle. May contain commas, so fold '(' .. ')' back into one field before indexing — and unlike AIS-140 this is NOT the last field.

fields.name: frame_number
fields.note: PROVISIONAL: 6-digit zero-padded sequence number, matching the AIS-140 frame_number format (its field 47). Read as a counter rather than an odometer because it advanced 000007 -> 000123 between two captures 22 minutes apart while the device reported 0.0 km/h throughout. Confirm against the vendor doc before treating it as distance.

can_id.note: zero-padded to 8 hex digits in the capture; values seen are 11-bit ids (0x0E1 .. 0x5B9). An id above 0x7FF is a 29-bit extended id.

payload.note: big-endian byte order as received off the bus; 16 hex chars = 8 bytes (a full CAN 2.0 frame) in every captured frame.

can_data.empty: the field is present but empty (two consecutive commas) when the packet carries no CAN data
can_data.note: Signal-level meaning is per vehicle, not per protocol: pair these frames with a DBC or CanPlus signature to scale them into engineering values (runway/convert/canplus.py). The parser therefore returns frames verbatim plus the derived numeric id / dlc, and does no scaling.

packet_type_codes.note: Inherited from the AIS-140 base packet; only NR has been observed on this model so far.

message_alert_ids.2: Location Update (history) — buffered while GPRS was unavailable
message_alert_ids.6: Alert – Connect back to main battery

source: Live capture from IMEI 868221073948609 (fw 5.1.29C, packet version V2.2.0) on 03-08-2026: the $LGN login plus $MMI NR sentences with and without CAN data, over a real TCP session at a 10 s reporting interval. No vendor protocol document available yet; the field mapping is derived from those samples against AIS140_Protocol_Description_v1.9, and every deviation/assumption is flagged in the field notes above.
